question: In the SNNOOP10 mnemonic for headache red flags, a thunderclap onset (reaching maximum intensity within 1 minute) is a red flag that mandates urgent neuroimaging to exclude subarachnoid haemorrhage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Thunderclap onset is the 'T' in SNNOOP10 and represents one of the highest-priority red flags. Any headache reaching maximum intensity within 1 minute must be presumed SAH until proven otherwise.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Thunderclap headache — reaching maximal severity within 60 seconds — is the classic presentation of subarachnoid haemorrhage and must be investigated urgently with non-contrast CT head, followed by LP ≥12 hours after onset if CT is negative.
